subject: EU tenant log export / retention — clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Ana Müller <ana.mueller@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeHealth Compliance <compliance@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU tenant log export / retention — initial questions

Hi Jordan,

We're preparing for our annual compliance package and need to confirm a few specifics about audit and access logs for our EU tenant hosted with Redwood. Can you confirm the following?

1) What's the default retention for access logs and for audit (admin) logs in the hosted EU environment?
2) Can you provide a bulk export of the last 3 years of audit events if requested by our auditors? If not, what's the maximum historical window available for hosted tenants?
3) What export formats are available (NDJSON/CSV/etc.) and do exports include raw event payloads or are some fields pseudonymized by default?
4) For deletion requests: will you provide a signed confirmation that PII in logs was removed and indicate the deletion timeline/process?
5) Are exports and deletion actions auditable (i.e., can we get an immutable trail that shows an export/deletion occurred)?

If possible, please include a sample schema or manifest so our auditors can validate. We're under a procurement timeline, so a response by EOD Thursday would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Ana Müller
Head of Compliance, AcmeHealth

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EU tenant log export / retention — detail and Q&A

Hi Ana — answering your points in order and adding some constraints so procurement and your auditors know what to expect.

1) Retention (hosted EU):
- Access logs (session/connectivity metadata): default 90 days for standard hosted tenants.
- Admin/audit logs (console actions, policy changes, token management): default 180 days.
- For Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments we can extend audit retention up to 7 years via contractual configuration (long-term retention is an add-on).

2) Historical bulk exports:
- Hosted tenants: we retain full event payloads per the retention windows above. We cannot export beyond the retention window for hosted tenants because the data is purged from primary storage per our retention enforcement.
- Dedicated/Private: with the long-term retention add-on or if you already have Dedicated, we can export up to 7 years of retained events.

3) Export formats and field fidelity:
- Primary export format for audit events: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — preserves full event payloads and nested fields.
- We provide CSV summaries for high-level access logs (session start/end, IP, principal id) for quick review.
- Exports include raw event fields by default for accounts with standard hosting. PII fields (user email, user_id) are included as plaintext unless a pseudonymization policy is applied for your account. Configuration options:
  * Full: raw fields included (default for most audit exports).
  * Pseudonymized: user identifiers hashed, IPs truncated to /24, email local-part redacted (for regulated reviewers).

4) Deletion and attestation:
- Deletion model: we perform a two-phase deletion for hosted tenants — a soft-delete (marker) followed by secure wipe from primary and secondary storage. Secure wipe timings: within 30 days from request for hosted accounts; within 7 days for Dedicated/Private where we control the storage configuration.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed deletion attestation (PDF) indicating which logical objects were removed and timestamps of the operation. For more sensitive requests we can produce an export manifest showing which objects were processed and include the cryptographic digest of the exported files.

5) Auditability of exports/deletions:
- All export and deletion actions are recorded in an immutable export-action ledger (append-only) for 12 months in hosted and up to the contract term in Dedicated/Private. The ledger includes requestor identity, request timestamp, job id, and resulting artifact checksums.

Notes/constraints:
- We do not retain raw access logs beyond the configured retention window for hosted tenants; if your audit requirements need longer windows we recommend Dedicated or the long-term retention add-on.
- Exports with raw payloads can contain sensitive fields — we recommend using our Customer-Managed Key option (bring-your-own-key) for encryption at rest if you need additional control.

I'll attach a small sample schema (NDJSON example) and a manifest CSV template for your auditors to review.

Attachment: sample_audit_export_schema.json (NDJSON example, 4KB)
Attachment: export_manifest_template.csv (CSV manifest, 1KB)

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-17T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: EU tenant log export / retention — export mechanics & SLA

Ana, quick ops notes to complement Laura's answers with concrete operational SLAs and naming conventions you can pass to auditors/procurement: 

- API & delivery: exports are requested via the Console (Export job) or the Exports API (POST /v1/exports). Jobs are tracked with job_id and manifest. If you prefer, we can run a one-off export and deliver to an S3-compatible endpoint in your EU account (requires S3 bucket + IAM role).
- Typical turn-times:
  * < 30 days of data: 24–72 hours.
  * 30–365 days: 3–7 business days.
  * > 365 days (hosted): not available — see Laura. For Dedicated/Private with long-term retention enabled: 5–15 business days depending on size.
- File format & packaging:
  * audit-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz (each day is a gzipped NDJSON file).
  * access-summary-YYYYMM.csv (daily rolled CSV summaries).
  * manifest-<job_id>.csv (records filename, object_count, sha256, compressed_size, encryption=aes256).
- Deliverables: we provide the archive(s), the manifest CSV, and a signed job receipt (PDF). All artifacts are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. For Private/Dedicated we support encryption with your KMS keys.
- File naming example: audit-acmehealth-eu-20270401-20270430-job-AB1234.ndjson.gz

I'll also note that exports over S3 require a pre-signed role and the export system will write directly into the supplied bucket; we do not persist a copy in Redwood after successful delivery unless configured to do so.

-Vivek
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
